title: Take orders from customers to fulfil a need for goods and/or service

lessons.title: Understanding the customer's need
lessons.html:
Understanding the customer's need

Taking an order is more than writing down what the customer asks for. A good order-taker makes sure the customer gets what they really need, in the right quantity, at the right time. In the seed business, an incorrect order can mean a farmer cannot plant on time, which costs far more than the price of the seed.

Ways orders arrive

  • Face to face, at a farm visit, co-op counter or farmer day
  • By phone or WhatsApp
  • By e-mail or written order form
  • Through an online ordering system
  • Through dealers and co-ops placing bulk orders

Finding the need

Ask open questions to understand what the customer wants to achieve:

  • What crop and how many hectares will you plant?
  • Dryland or irrigation? What planting window?
  • What plant population do you plan? (This decides seed quantity.)
  • Which cultivars did you use before, and how did they perform?
  • When and where must the seed be delivered?

Calculating quantity

Seed for maize is usually sold in bags of a set number of seeds. A simple calculation helps: hectares multiplied by target plants per hectare, divided by seeds per bag, then add a small allowance for germination and field losses as the agronomist advises. Example: 100 ha at 40 000 plants per hectare needs 4 000 000 plants; at 80 000 seeds per bag that is 50 bags before allowance. Show the customer the calculation so they understand.

Advising

If the requested product does not suit the customer's conditions, explain this politely and suggest alternatives. If the product is out of stock, offer a suitable substitute and let the customer decide. Never substitute without the customer's agreement.

lessons.title: Processing the order
lessons.html:
Processing the order

Once the need is clear, the order must be captured accurately and passed on so that it can be fulfilled.

Information on the order

ItemExample
Customer name, account number, contact detailsFrom the customer database
Product, cultivar, treatment, pack sizeExact product code
QuantityNumber of bags or kg
Price and discountsFrom the current price list
Payment termsCash, account, harvest credit
Delivery address and dateFarm name, GPS pin, directions
Special instructionsGate times, offloading equipment

Steps

  1. Check stock availability in the system before confirming.
  2. Check the customer's credit status or arrange payment.
  3. Read the order back to the customer and confirm every detail.
  4. Capture the order in the system correctly and give the customer an order number.
  5. Send written confirmation, such as an e-mail or order copy.
  6. Pass the order to the warehouse and dispatch team.

After the order

  • Track the order and inform the customer about delays immediately, with a new date.
  • Confirm delivery and check that the customer is satisfied.
  • Handle changes or cancellations according to company policy, and record them.

Professional conduct

Be honest about delivery times and prices. Do not push customers to buy more than they need. Protect their personal and financial information in line with POPIA. A customer who trusts you will come back season after season.

Key points

  • Ask questions to find the real need before writing the order.
  • Calculate quantities from hectares and plant population and show the customer.
  • Check stock and credit before confirming.
  • Read the order back and send written confirmation.
  • Track the order and inform the customer of any delay.
